findings.claim: MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T> no longer throws TypeAccessException for types without a known hash-resistant comparer. It now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default, so with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData an attacker-controlled dictionary or hash-set key of any unlisted type uses a collision-prone comparer. This silently removes the hash-collision-resistance protection (hash-flooding DoS). It is unrelated to the formatter feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, call GetEqualityComparer<T>() for a custom key type with no known hash-resistant comparer (e.g. a user struct). Assert it throws TypeAccessException. The test passes on base and fails on head. Alternatively deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKey,int> under UntrustedData and expect TypeAccessException.
